verses.text: On the twenty-first day of the seventh month, the LORD gave this message through the prophet Haggai:
"Speak to Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, the governor of Judah, to Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest, and to the rest of the people. Ask them,
'Is there anyone left among you who saw this house in its former glory? How does it look to you now? Doesn't it seem like nothing to you?

But now be strong, Zerubbabel,' says the LORD. 'Be strong, Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest. Be strong, all you people of the land,' says the LORD. 'Get to work, because I am with you,' says the LORD of Armies.
'This is what I promised you when you came out of Egypt. My Spirit remains among you. Do not be afraid.'
"This is what the LORD of Armies says: 'In a little while I will once more shake the heavens and the earth, the sea and the dry land.
I will shake all the nations, and the treasures of all the nations will come here. I will fill this house with glory,' says the LORD of Armies.
'The silver is mine, and the gold is mine,' says the LORD of Armies.
'The glory of this new house will be greater than the glory of the old one,' says the LORD of Armies. 'And in this place I will give peace,' says the LORD of Armies."
On the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month, in the second year of Darius, the LORD gave this message through the prophet Haggai:
"This is what the LORD of Armies says: Ask the priests what the law says.
'Suppose someone carries holy meat in the fold of his clothes, and the fold touches some bread, stew, wine, olive oil, or other food. Does that food become holy?'" The priests answered, "No."
Then Haggai asked, "Suppose someone who is unclean from touching a dead body touches any of these things. Does it become unclean?" The priests answered, "Yes, it becomes unclean."
Then Haggai said, "'That is how these people and this nation look to me,' says the LORD. 'Whatever they do and whatever they offer there is unclean.
Now think carefully about how things were before today, before one stone was laid on another in the LORD's temple.
Back then, when someone came to a pile of grain expecting twenty measures, there were only ten. When someone came to the wine vat to draw out fifty measures, there were only twenty.
I struck everything you did with blight, mildew, and hail, yet you did not turn back to me,' says the LORD.
'Think carefully about this day and the days before it, from this twenty-fourth day of the ninth month, the day the foundation of the LORD's temple was laid. Think carefully.
Is there still any seed left in the barn? Until now the vine, the fig tree, the pomegranate, and the olive tree have produced nothing. But from this day on I will bless you.'"
The LORD gave a second message to Haggai on the twenty-fourth day of the month:
"Tell Zerubbabel, the governor of Judah, 'I am going to shake the heavens and the earth.

I will overturn royal thrones and destroy the power of the kingdoms of the nations. I will overturn chariots and their drivers. Horses and their riders will fall, each one killed by the sword of his companion.

"'On that day,' says the LORD of Armies, 'I will take you, my servant Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel,' says the LORD, 'and I will make you like my signet ring, because I have chosen you,' says the LORD of Armies."
